correctness.rationale: For a centered simplex, the zonotope support is one half of the l1 norm of the vertex projection vector. For each edge, a unit normal to the span of the other d-1 vertices makes all other projections vanish; the zero-sum relation leaves two opposite coefficients, giving a support value at most half that edge length. The inradius is the minimum support value because the zonotope is centrally symmetric. Hence every edge is at least twice the inradius, giving the global 1/2 bound, stability, and equality rigidity. The regular converse follows from the exact published strip description. The package checker independently replays the special-direction identities and regular tight case.

value.rationale: The Euclidean ball is the canonical symmetric diameter-one test body in Makeev's universal-cover problem, and the accepted theorem identifies the unique generator that is best possible for this test under the conjecture's own diameter normalization. The edgewise estimate is structural rather than merely numerical: near-maximal inradius forces every simplex edge near the common extremal length, giving an immediate stability statement.
